incident.description:
# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

Synthetic evaluation record derived from a historical incident. Not an actual company record or operating instruction.

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported in this evaluation case.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

Synthetic evaluation record. All equipment identifiers and layout details are fictional and are not operating instructions.

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

documents.extractedText:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

Synthetic evaluation record. Conventions apply to this fictional case only.

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

documents.extractedText:
# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

Synthetic evaluation record. Fictional administrative requirements, not the partner's actual policy or a safe-work procedure.

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

payload.summary:
At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024 (Turn 2), a two-person Utilities crew (U-A/U-B) was preparing for planned maintenance of the #1 slab caster dryer group in the RHOB process area. They had collected work folder WO-527 but had not yet received formal release/maintenance acceptance from Maintenance receiver M-A, nor completed boundary preparation.

At ~10:00 AM, an air-low indication occurred at the RHOB service station (Receiving header H-R). The crew paused work. By 10:07 AM, local indications returned to normal without a formal line opening or restoration procedure documented in this packet yet.
payload.focalEvent: Loss of instrument-air pressure indicated by an alarm/indication at the RHOB service station while maintenance preparation was underway but not released.
payload.actualImpact: Work paused; no injuries reported. Air supply restored within ~7 minutes (10:02-10:07).
payload.potentialImpact: Loss of instrument air could have caused unintended valve movements, loss of control for safety systems, or inability to isolate equipment if a failure had persisted.
payload.normalState: Utilities operations manages the North gallery and Dryer aisle; RHOB operations observes receiving header H-R. Normal pressure is in 'local band' (numeric value unknown).
payload.eventState: At event time: Utilities crew at gallery preparing boundary; Maintenance receiver present but acceptance not signed/recorded as complete; no temporary instruction attached to WO-527.

Crew U-A/U-B had operating qualifications and energy-control authorization at shift start.
Work order WO-527 was scheduled for planned maintenance of dryer group D-101.
unknowns: Exact time the air pressure dropped (approximate 'About 10:00' in log).
Whether the interruption originated at source, distribution system, or receiving equipment.
Numeric value of low-pressure alarm threshold and normal band limits.
Specific valve positions during the event.
Reason for air restoration (automatic vs manual intervention not yet detailed).
Status of any change records affecting service routing on May 20.
Whether a temporary instruction was required but missing.

questions.intent: Determine if the interruption originated upstream or downstream to clarify causal chain and responsible system boundary.
questions.text: Did pressure monitoring at any point between the air source (North gallery) and RHOB receiving header H-R show a drop before, during, or after 10:00 AM? If so, where was the first indication of loss?
questions.rationale: Distinguishes whether Utilities distribution failed versus an isolated event affecting only RHOB.
evidenceNeeded: Pressure trend logs for North gallery and Dryer aisle between 09:35-10:20.
Alarm export times vs acknowledgment times from IA-S01.
questions.causalBranch: System boundary of failure (Source vs Distribution vs Receiving)

questions.intent: Verify if maintenance release/boundary acceptance was formally completed before the event.
questions.text: Was Maintenance receiver M-A's signature on WO-527 obtained and recorded prior to 10:00 AM? If not, what specific boundary conditions were assumed or communicated verbally?
questions.rationale: Determines if work proceeded without formal acceptance of energy boundaries, which is a procedural gap.
evidenceNeeded: Signed copy of WO-527 maintenance release form (if exists).
Interview with M-A regarding verbal agreements.

questions.intent: Identify if any recent changes to instrument-air routing or equipment configuration were in effect on May 20.
questions.text: Were there any change records (ECP revisions, drawing redlines) affecting the RHOB service station or Dryer aisle active between March and April 2024 that might explain a transient loss?
questions.rationale: Change management failures often cause unexpected behavior in energy systems.
evidenceNeeded: List of issued change records effective May 20, 2024.
Engineering disposition documents for any routing changes.

questions.intent: Clarify the mechanism and duration of air restoration.
questions.text: Was pressure restored automatically by a redundant supply, manual valve operation, or system reset? Who performed any action between 10:02 AM and 10:07 AM?
questions.rationale: Understanding restoration helps assess risk recurrence and whether safeguards were adequate.
evidenceNeeded: Field notes from U-A/U-B/M-A regarding actions taken.
Valve position records or SCADA snapshots.

decision.summary: The incident involved a transient loss of instrument air at the RHOB service station during maintenance preparation. The crew had not yet received formal release/maintenance acceptance, and no temporary instruction was attached to WO-527. Key unknowns include the origin of the pressure drop (source vs distribution), exact timing relative to boundary status, and whether any recent changes affected system behavior.
unknowns: Exact pressure drop origin and timing.
Formal maintenance release status at event time.
Recent change records affecting routing.
alternatives: Pressure loss was a brief upstream fluctuation unrelated to the work area.
Loss occurred due to an unrecorded valve misposition during preparation.
A recent but undocumented change altered normal operation.
